evidence.quote:
| process | `CC1 VIN1 ...` | recombine node (MNM2 drain) | MNM6 gate |
| 1 | `n2` | `n0` | `n8` |
| 2 | `n4` | `n2` | `n6` |
| 3 | `n2` | `n6` | `n7` |
| 4 | `n5` | `n3` | `n9` |
the symptom that exposed it was one deck text giving 35.94 / 30.26 / 25.24 dB S21 in three different processes while the untouched design replayed at exactly 35.961 every time.
**element names are the contract, node names are an implementation detail**, and every future netlist-post-processing tool in this tree needs to know it.

rule: Resolve every circuit role in a netlist post-processor from element names, cross-checked against a second element that must touch the node, and raise rather than guess when the contract drifts.

applicability.applies: Every insertion tool: switch banks, balun grafts, probe injection, linearization taps. Element names (CC*, LL*, MNM*, RR*) and the fixed nets (VIN1, VOUT1, p1, p2, VDD) ARE stable; internal n<k> names are not.
applicability.not: One work package. The failure is silent -- the deck runs and returns a plausible number every time -- so the absence of an error is not evidence the tool is attached correctly.
